test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Mukesh sold a car for ₹1,20,000 at 40% loss. For what price (in ₹) should he sell the carto gain 55% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio method: Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100%.

First selling price (SP₁) = 100% − 40% = 60%.

Desired selling price (SP₂) = 100% + 55% = 155%.

Given: 60% → 1,20,000. So, 1% → 1,20,000 ÷ 60 = 2,000.

Required SP₂ = 155 × 2,000 = 3,10,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,10,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹1,20,000, Loss% = 40%, Required Profit% = 55%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%); SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd6d67ac03e9e7cb2ab4cb9110605313ab7bb8634d24bd7554b59299885b10d3.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 1,20,000 × 100 ÷ (100 − 40) = 1,20,000 × 100 ÷ 60.

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 2,00,000.

⇒ **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 2,00,000 × (100 + 55) ÷ 100.

⇒ **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 2,00,000 × 155 ÷ 100 = 2,000 × 155.

⇒ **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 3,10,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,10,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

When an object is sold at a loss, the **Cost Price** is always greater than the **Selling Price**. CP = SP + Loss.

Direct SP Calculation

To find the new SP directly: SP₂ = SP₁ × (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Loss%).
